etymologies.etymologyHTML: From dis- +‎ belief.

definitions.definition: Unpreparedness, unwillingness, or inability to believe that something is the case.
The loss or abandonment of a belief; cessation of belief.

quote.citation: 1885, H. J. Hardwicke, “The God Idea”, in The Agnostic: A Monthly Journal of Liberal Thought, volume 1, page 239:
quote.text: There is an agony of suffering in that lingering doubt which haunts the human soul in the beginnings of disbelief.

quote.citation: 1927, Gilbert W. Gabriel, “Male, Female and American Drama”, in Vanity Fair, volume 27, number 4, page 73:
quote.text: No adolescent can achieve disbelief in the stork without an eruption of young oaths and cynicisms.

quote.citation: 2002, Laikwan Pang, Building a New China in Cinema: The Chinese Left-wing Cinema Movement, 1932-1937, →ISBN, page 99:
quote.text: His later left-wing films prevented any pure and strong emotional attachment between the two sexes from gaining narrative momentum, which might reflect his gradual disbelief in romantic love.

quote.citation: 2012, Gloria Neufeld Redekop, Bad Girls and Boys Go to Hell (or not): Engaging Fundamentalist Evangelicalism, →ISBN, page 246:
quote.text: Just like the disbelief in Santa Claus happens gradually, I wondered if it was similar for people leaving their faith.
